title: Regional customer summary: aggregate before joining wide rows
prompt: Quarterly account-manager report. Region 1 (about 700k customers, 1.1M orders and 4.4M lines per quarter) takes
about 3.5 minutes. The plan carries AccountNumber and LastName through the joins into a hash aggregate that spills
about 2.4 GB to tempdb, and COUNT(DISTINCT) adds a second aggregation branch. The report must list every customer
in the region, including those with no orders in the quarter (OrderCount 0, Revenue NULL). Orders with no lines
count as orders but add no revenue.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
OrderLines: 120M rows, 4 per order on average. About 0.3% of orders have no lines.
baseline_sql: LEFT JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID

correct_families.description: Group by the narrow keys first (order, then customer) and join the wide customer columns afterwards with an outer join.
reference_sql: JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID AND c.RegionID = @RegionID
LEFT JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(Revenue) AS Revenue
LEFT JOIN CustAgg a ON a.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

traps.why: The date and status predicates in the outer WHERE turn the LEFT JOIN into an inner join. Customers with no orders in the quarter disappear.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer in the region with no order in the quarter.
example_sql: LEFT JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
LEFT JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID

traps.why: The report shows Revenue NULL for a customer with no orders or only orders without lines. ISNULL turns it into 0.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer in the region with no order in the quarter.
example_sql: JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID AND c.RegionID = @RegionID
LEFT JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(Revenue) AS Revenue
LEFT JOIN CustAgg a ON a.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

traps.why: An inner join to OrderLines drops orders that have no lines, so OrderCount is too low.
traps.told_apart_by: An order in the quarter that has no lines (0.3% of orders).

JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID

min_improvement.basis: Provisional: no reference measurement. The 2.4 GB spill and the second aggregation branch must go.
